A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TreeGrad-Ranker and contain readable main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be reliably matched across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H report original feature-ranking experiments, numerical-error measurements, runtime comparisons, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G retain those original experiments and additionally report numerical-error results for path-dependent TreeShap.

M1.justification: TreeGrad, TreeGrad-Ranker, TreeGrad-Shap, and TreeProb retain their algorithmic steps and objectives. Matching relocated pseudocode establishes that the additions are explanatory comments, not procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine classification/regression datasets and Click prediction small for numerical-error experiments. Decision-tree, boosted-tree, and predicted/non-predicted-class scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Figure 5(b) adds path-dependent TreeShap, implemented in the SHAP package, to the numerical-error comparison. This is distinct from the existing TreeShap-K discussion. Other numerical comparators and feature-ranking baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The splits, metrics, sample counts, tree configurations, and optimization settings are retained. TreeShap joins the existing error-versus-depth evaluation. Revised captions clarify per-instance Beta-Shapley selection without establishing a changed selection procedure.

E4.justification: Figure 5(b) extends the numerical-stability analysis to path-dependent TreeShap. Existing analyses of quadrature-node choices, runtime, and sensitivity to iteration count and learning rate remain.

E5.justification: The fixed seed, five-instance numerical-error averages, 200-instance ranking/runtime averages, and stated runtime standard-deviation reporting are unchanged. Figure 5(b) changes shaded-band values but documents no change in statistical estimation or reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 5(b) adds TreeShap errors around 10^-14, compared with TreeGrad-Shap errors around 10^-15. Existing mean curves are retained, but their shaded bands change. Other experimental plots and table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Space-complexity statements change from tight Θ bounds to O upper bounds, including Corollary 1. The vectorized TreeGrad-Shap description changes from Θ(min(D,N)^2 + L) to O(D^2 + L). Definitions, central theorems, and proof arguments otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about probabilistic-value limitations, O(L) gradients, feature-score axioms, numerical stability, and ranking performance.

C2.justification: The appendix changes TreeGrad-Shap from the 'only numerically stable algorithm' to the 'most numerically stable algorithm' alongside the added TreeShap comparison. Other mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the SHAP implementation and its source link, explicitly clarifies per-instance Beta-Shapley selection, and adds comments specifying elementwise operations and the quadrature interval in vectorized pseudocode. Existing implementation settings and access information are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but v2 explicitly compares numerical stability against the already cited path-dependent TreeShap of Lundberg et al. (2020) and qualifies the corresponding uniqueness claim.

P1.justification: v2 adds an appendix contents list, removes the LLM-use statement, relabels scientific appendices B–H as A–G, rearranges algorithm presentations, and lightly edits prose and captions. The main narrative is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 5(b) gains a TreeShap curve and legend entry, revised shading, and changed logarithmic-axis ticks. Figure 5, Table 1, and several pseudocode blocks move; captions are clarified. Other experimental graphics retain their content.

improvement.justification: Adding the established TreeShap comparator and qualifying the numerical-stability interpretation modestly strengthen the paper's evidence and precision. Baseline-selection clarification and appendix navigation also help. Gains are limited: methods and existing mean results remain unchanged, while altered shaded bands are unexplained and some algorithm-line references become stale after renumbering.
